key_insight: Low DFT energy and force errors do not guarantee reliable dynamics in disordered carbon; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust foundation potential tested.
engineering_relevance: Application-specific validation is essential before using foundation interatomic potentials to simulate nanoporous carbon, especially with oxygen and hydrogen present.
method: Screen six foundation potentials against DFT energies, forces and binding curves.
Test four potentials with melt–quench–anneal molecular dynamics.
Evaluate structural observables in pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons.
evidence_signal: Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures, while all four dynamics-tested models reproduced principal experimental and specialised-potential signatures of nanoporous carbon.
watch_item: Shared structural biases among OMAT-based models suggest that training coverage can limit reliability despite architectural differences.
paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
